title: Coefficient-compatible open extension base change and its exact derived comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$ and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be admissible [sk-def-localizing-closure], using [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. On a small representative of each small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $\mathcal C_T=\Mod_{\Lambda_T}(\Sh(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Ab))$, where $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients; sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $r:W\to\overline Y$ and let $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ be a quasi-compact open immersion. Put $U=W\times_{\overline Y}Y$, with projections $j:U\hookrightarrow W$ and $p:U\to Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product; def-weil-open-immersion]. Write $f^{-1}$ for abelian inverse image, $\alpha_f:f^{-1}\Lambda_{\mathrm{target}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{\mathrm{source}}$ for the canonical coefficient map [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], and
$$c:j^{-1}r^{-1}\Lambda_{\overline Y}\xrightarrow{\sim}p^{-1}i^{-1}\Lambda_{\overline Y}$$
for the fixed inverse-image square comparison [def-sf-proetale-ring-sheaf-operations]. Then the two maps from $p^{-1}i^{-1}\Lambda_{\overline Y}$ to $\Lambda_U$ agree:
$$\alpha_j\circ j^{-1}(\alpha_r)\circ c^{-1}=\alpha_p\circ p^{-1}(\alpha_i).$$
Use the actual module functors $f^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{-1})$ and $h_!=h^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_h}$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback; sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. The arbitrary-ring open comparison of [lem-sf-ring-sheaf-base-change-mates], after the canonical scalar identifications $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha^{-1}}$ [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso], is a natural $\Lambda_W$-linear isomorphism
$$\beta:r^*i_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!p^*: \mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_W.$$
Let $\theta:p^*i^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*r^*$ be the fixed module pullback-square comparison given by the composition isomorphisms for $rj=ip$. The adjunct of $\beta_T^{-1}:j_!p^*T\to r^*i_!T$ under the specified $j_!\dashv j^*$ is $\theta_{i_!T}\circ p^*(u_{i,T})$, where $u_i$ is the specified open unit. All four functors are exact. On ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], exact termwise localization with its canonical composition comparisons [lem-sfb-exact-derived-natural-iso; lem-sfb-exact-derived-composition] gives a natural isomorphism
$$\beta_D:D(r^*)D(i_!)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(j_!)D(p^*).$$
Its component on a complex is the localization of the degreewise $\beta$ under the exact-functor factorizations; it commutes with every canonical integer shift. No properness, boundedness or constructibility is required.

Exact descent uses categories.tex Tag 04VG, label lemma-properties-left-localization. The full scalar-transport argument is preserved in report.md.

proof.text: Prove the generic symmetry equation upperStarCompIso(h).symm = upperStarCompIso(h.symm), using inversion of composites and the equality-transport congruence symmetry equation proved by equality induction. Rewrite the inverse of the fixed ring-sheaf square comparison by this equation. Apply the square clause of the existing proved profinite_point_pullback_abelian_coherence to b=p, f=i, fprime=j, g=r and pullback.condition.symm. Unfold only the square comparison and the condensed coefficient abbreviations and normalize composition associativity. This gives exactly the displayed coefficient equation, without reducing equality transports between concrete inverse-image functors. The ring-sheaf comparison has a proved construction equation. Use its inverse-component equation to specialize the generic coefficient identity. Explicit congruence equations convert the point-comparison components to the named condensed coefficient maps, avoiding kernel reduction of the comparison through sheafification.

proof.text: Construct t:p^* followed by j_! to i_! followed by r^* componentwise as the inverse Hom-equivalence applied to p^*(unit_i) followed by the specified module square comparison. Naturality follows from naturality of the Hom-equivalence, unit and square comparison. This construction fixes the desired adjunct from the outset.

source.place: Proof (4), open base change by adjunction; exact localization uses Stacks Tag 04VG.

proof.text: The open module unit is invertible: module extension by zero is fully faithful, by the existing fully faithful linear lift of abelian extension by zero and the coefficient restriction equivalence. Extension along the invertible coefficient map identifies the underlying sheaf of r^*i_!T with the ordinary abelian pullback of i_!T. Existing ordinary sheaf open base change identifies this with an extension by zero along j. The existing module essential-image criterion lifts this sheaf support statement to module objects. Thus the specified module counit on r^*i_!T is invertible. The inverse Hom-equivalence is j_! applied to the unit-square composite followed by this counit; all factors are invertible. Set beta=(asIso t).symm. Applying the Hom-equivalence to its inverse component gives exactly the required adjunct equation.

source.place: Proof (4), open base change by adjunction; exact localization uses Stacks Tag 04VG.

proof.text: All eight finite-limit/finite-colimit properties are the existing exactness instances for module pullback and module open extension. For four exact additive functors F,R,P,J, form the termwise natural isomorphism C(F)C(R) to C(P)C(J) from beta and the canonical termwise composition comparisons. The factorization isomorphisms of exact derived functors turn this into an isomorphism after precomposition by Q. The localization fully faithful whiskering functor supplies its preimage isomorphism beta_D. The map-preimage equality, evaluated at K, and cancellation of the factorization isomorphism yield the exact displayed normalization.

source.place: Proof (4), open base change by adjunction; exact localization uses Stacks Tag 04VG.

proof.text: Termwise natural transformations and composition comparisons commute with every integer shift, as do the exact derived factorization isomorphisms. Their composite after Q therefore commutes with shifts. Since Q is essentially surjective, NatTrans.CommShift.of_whiskerLeft gives the shift compatibility of beta_D itself.

The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged and there is no re-split note. The nine-step proof was read against the statement of every cited node. Step 1: transposing lem-sfb-eta-comp gives alpha_a a^{-1}alpha_b = alpha_{ba} m_{a,b}; c = m_{p,i}^{-1} m_{j,r}, confirmed against the upperStarCompIso definition (Iso.lean:119); the cocycle has the right orientation. Step 2: the e_a fixed by its unit (Res_a(e)u = id) via conjugate-iso-unit-equation is the same leftAdjointUniq construction as def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso (extendScalarsIsoComapInv). Step 3: every hypothesis of lem-sf-ring-sheaf-base-change-mates holds (qcqs-over-affine, reduced induced complement, qc open, arbitrary ring object). Step 4: I recomputed the restriction chain; the composite scalar map p^{-1}alpha_i c j^{-1}alpha_r^{-1} equals alpha_p^{-1}alpha_j by step 1, using projection-formula-comap with identity carriers. Step 5: the module compositor is fixed by its conjugate, with the abelian carrier (lower-star-comp), and the transported unit is u_i by the linearization-transport Hom bijection. Step 6: the transpose of beta^{-1} uses the stated mate formula, direction checked. Step 7: pullback is exact by cartesian-coefficients (including the condensed Q-bar coefficient) and j_! is exact. Steps 8-9: the unbounded exact-derived natural-iso, composition and factorization statements give beta_D and its shift squares (tau = id, sign (-1)^n preserved). Edge cases checked: i = id, Y empty, r = id, T = 0, negative odd n. lem-sfb-integral-bounded-stratum-base-change (O_E, D^b) is narrower, not a duplicate. The tool uses recorded in split_report (generic module, adjunction and derived tools; ring-sheaf mates, eta-comp, cartesian-coefficients used as black boxes) are accepted for the maintainer. Advisory only: step 4 leaves implicit that mapModLeft equals j^lin_! (the same projection-formula linearization). No SGA is cited. No changes.
